meta.notes: Initial pack. Every required field carries at least two strategies of different kinds (TR-SEL-010), ordered most-stable-first. Selectors here are structural patterns rather than a transcription of any particular rendering; they are validated against the fixture corpus in PH-13, and staged per the six-step rollout in selectors/README.md before any client uses them.

strategies.notes: Each review is exposed as an article to assistive technology. This is a user-facing accessibility contract, so it changes rarely and never quietly — a vendor that broke it would break screen readers first, which is a louder failure for them than for us.

The vendor's own review identifier, used by their client-side code. Stable while their tooling depends on it, which is why it ranks above anything structural, but it is theirs to rename without notice.

The accessible label carries the author name as a value rather than as rendered text, so it survives a visual redesign that changes how the name is displayed. Ranked first because it gives the value directly.

The contributor link inside a review container. Survives class renames because it keys on the href shape, and breaks only if the container layout is restructured — which is a bigger change than a restyle.

Last resort. Fastest to write and first to break; present so a redesign that takes out both strategies above degrades to a working fallback rather than to a quarantined record. Its use should show up in the strategy histogram as a signal to re-author the pack.

The star widget's accessible label states the numeric rating. Vastly more robust than counting filled star glyphs, which changes with every icon-set revision and is locale-independent here because the number is in the label regardless of the surrounding words.
The vendor's own rating attribute. Ranked below the aria label because it is internal tooling rather than a user-facing contract, so it carries no external pressure against renaming.
Scoped fallback for renderings where the star widget is not the first labelled image. Structure-dependent, so it survives restyling but not a layout rewrite.
The review body. Optional because a rating-only review is legitimate and common; a null here is real data rather than an extraction failure.
The body is the element carrying a language attribute, which the vendor sets so translation can be offered. Doubles as a language hint when the detector is uncertain.
Sources publish relative dates, not absolute ones. This reads the accessible label, which states it in full where the visible text is sometimes abbreviated to '2mo'.

Locale-dependent by nature — this is the English form and the pack is per-locale — but structure-independent, so it survives any amount of markup churn. Ranked below the aria label precisely because of that locale dependence.
The business's reply. Optional: most reviews have none, so absence is ordinary rather than a failure.
The reply is introduced by a fixed phrase. Locale-dependent, and ranked last because a false match would attribute the owner's words to the reviewer — which is worse than reporting no reply at all.

challenge.notes: A challenge is TERMINAL and never retried (INV-07). Detected structurally rather than by status code, because the challenge is served as a 200.

empty_state.notes: Distinguishes a listing with genuinely no reviews from a page that failed to render them. Without it, both look like zero reviews — and one of those is a reason to publish nothing while the other is a reason to raise ERR-PARSE-EMPTY-UNEXPECTED (CH-06).

consent.notes: The consent interstitial hides the review list entirely. Medium confidence because the phrases are generic enough to appear in ordinary page content.
